title: Age Calculator for Completed Years, Days Lived, and Birthdays
description: Enter birth and reference dates for age and days since birth. Use leap-day and month-end examples to verify birthday countdowns, year-based age, and errors.
content:
Open the age calculator and enter your date of birth in “Date of birth.” Set “Age as of” to the date you want to look up. The result updates automatically once both dates are complete. You can also select “Calculate.” The large “Completed years” value shows how many full years have passed. The breakdown below shows the additional months and days.

Enter your date of birth and reference date

Open the age calculator and find “Your inputs.” The page fills in “Age as of” using your device’s local date and pre-fills “Date of birth” with a sample. Even if the page already shows a result, replace the sample with your own date. To calculate your age today, verify the reference date and leave it as is.

The reference date determines when your age is measured. For an old group photo, enter the date it was taken. For your age at an event, enter the event date and read “Completed years.” If the result shows dashes after an edit, read the message in the input section and verify the year, month, and day in each field. Select the year first, then verify the month and day to avoid accidentally choosing your birth day of the month in the current month.

  • Enter your date of birth as a Gregorian year, month, and day.
  • Set “Age as of” to the date you want to look up.
  • Before reading the result, compare the fields to verify that the dates are in the right places.

To compare two results, keep the date of birth fixed and change the reference date for each calculation. Record the reference date with each result. Repeating an earlier calculation with the same inputs helps you tell whether a discrepancy comes from the dates entered or from copying the wrong result field.

Completed years counts full years of age

If you know only the birth year, subtracting the years leaves out whether the birthday has passed. France’s National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies distinguishes age based on the year of birth from age in completed years at the most recent birthday. [S5] The US CDC also defines age in completed years at the most recent birthday and allows the survey or interview date to serve as the reference date. [S1]

Use the same date of birth for both calculations. Enter 2000-02-29 as the date of birth and 2025-02-27 as the reference date. “Completed years” shows 24. Change only the reference date to 2025-02-28, and the value becomes 25. For this leap-day birthday, the tool uses the last day of February in non-leap years. Changing only the reference date lets you see the effect of that single day on the completed age.

Read years, months, and days alongside total days

The breakdown below the large number can help you caption old photos. Photos from the same year can show the same completed age. The years, months, and days tell readers how far past the birthday each photo was taken. The United Nations Statistics Division glossary also distinguishes units. Age in years uses completed years, while the age of younger children can also be expressed in months, weeks, or days. [S6]

“Days since birth” shows the total days elapsed from the date of birth to the reference date. To verify it, enter the same start and end dates in the date difference calculator and leave “Include both dates” cleared. When the start and end are the same date, zero days have elapsed. To see how far apart two photos were taken, enter their dates directly in the date difference calculator.

Date of birth Age as of Completed years and age breakdown Days since birth
2000-02-29 2025-02-27 24 years, with a breakdown of 24 years, 11 months, and 29 days 9,130 days
2000-02-29 2025-02-28 25 years, with a breakdown of 25 years, 0 months, and 0 days 9,131 days
2025-01-31 2025-02-28 0 years, with a breakdown of 0 years, 1 month, and 0 days 28 days

If the total is one day higher when you verify it, look at “Include both dates” on the date difference page. Selecting it counts the start date as well. The age calculator shows elapsed days, so identical start and end dates give zero.

How whole months work for births at month end

Try the month-end example from the table. Set the date of birth to 2025-01-31 and “Age as of” to 2025-02-28. February has no matching day of the month, so the tool uses the last day of February. By that date, 1 whole month has elapsed. To see how the two values in the table are calculated, mark both dates on a calendar. Verify that the whole-month mark has been reached, then count the calendar days between the dates.

To work out the years, months, and remaining days by hand, count forward from the date of birth in whole months and find the latest monthly mark on or before the reference date. If a month has no matching day, use its last day. Use the original birth day of the month each time, so that months with a matching day use that original day again. Count the days from the latest mark to the reference date to get the remainder. This method is especially useful for verifying photo dates that span the end of a month.

How the calculator handles leap-day birthdays

February ends on different dates in leap and non-leap years. The month table in RFC 3339 lists both dates. [S2] The ECMAScript specification also describes the Gregorian calendar rules it uses to map dates. [S4] For someone born on February 29, this tool uses February 28 as the birthday in non-leap years. The rule appears below the inputs. To verify the result, keep the original leap day as the date of birth and adjust the reference date on the right.

In the earlier example, change the reference date from the day before the birthday to the birthday itself. “Completed years” increases by one year, and “Days to birthday” becomes 0 days. “Next birthday” still shows that date, with “Birthday today” on the right. For a reference date in the past, “today” means the date you selected. Read the completed age and birthday date together to verify that both change at the end of February in a non-leap year.

Find the next birthday from the reference date

To see how far a weekend is from your birthday, set the reference date to that weekend and read “Days to birthday.” If the birthday is still ahead, “Next birthday” shows the birthday in the reference year. Once it has passed, the tool shows the following year’s birthday. On the birthday itself, the tool still shows that date and switches the following day. Compare the birthday with the day after. The next birthday can move into the next year, while the days since birth increase by one day.

The progress bar shows how much of the current birthday cycle has passed. It fills on the birthday and drops back toward the start the following day. Compare the bar with the date alongside it. For the number of days remaining, read the value in days next to “Days to birthday.” To get the current countdown again, set the reference date to your device’s current date.

Why year-based age can exceed completed years

“Year-based age” subtracts the birth year from the reference year and adds 1. Changing the month or day leaves this value unchanged as long as both years stay the same. In the leap-day example, year-based age is 26 both the day before the birthday and on the birthday. The large completed-years value and the breakdown below it change. Read the results side by side to make sure you use the intended field.

If you organize photos in a table, label the column with the measure you use, either completed years or year-based age. You can then verify which measure each row uses when you sort the records by age. If two records disagree, compare their dates of birth and reference dates first, then compare the result fields they use. For photos spanning several years, keep the original photo dates so you can reproduce the age calculations.

You can also keep the date of birth fixed and move the reference date to the same month and day in the following year to see how both measures change. For a birthday other than leap day, the completed age increases by one year on the same date in the new year. For the leap-day example, use the birthday date shown by the tool.

Limits and invalid dates

The tool accepts Gregorian dates with a year, month, and day, from 0001-01-01 through 9999-12-31. If you have a lunar birth date, use the lunar calendar converter to find the corresponding Gregorian date in the year of birth, then enter that date. If you know only the birth year, you need the month and day to determine which birthdays have passed. The inputs have no hours or minutes fields, and the tool calculates by calendar day.

The HTML specification requires the browser’s date input to clear invalid date values. [S3] If a field is blank or the date of birth is after the reference date, the page displays “Choose valid dates. Birth cannot be after the reference date.” The large number is replaced by a dash, and “Copy result” is unavailable. You can enter the same date in both fields. Completed years and days since birth both show 0. If the reference date is in the last supported year and that year’s birthday has passed, “Next birthday” and “Days to birthday” show dashes.

If you see the error, look for a blank date first, then compare the years. If they match, compare the months and days. Once you correct the dates, the values replace the dashes. You can then copy the corrected dates and results together.

Verify the dates and results before copying

Select “Copy result” to paste the calculation into your notes. The copied text starts with the date of birth and reference date, followed by age in years, months, and days, total days since birth, and the next birthday. To keep the year-based age or days to birthday, record them separately from the corresponding fields and include the reference date. If you later need to verify a day count, the same note will have the dates you used.

When reviewing an old result, read the reference date at the top first. If a birthday has passed since then, the old completed age is out of date. To update it, enter the original date of birth and set “Age as of” to the date you want to look up. Before recording the new result, verify that the breakdown below the large number comes from the calculation for the two dates in your notes.

faqs.q: How do I find my age in completed years on a past date?
faqs.a: Select that date in “Age as of” and enter your date of birth as a Gregorian year, month, and day. Read the large “Completed years” value in the results.

faqs.q: Why does the tool show “Birthday today” on my birthday?
faqs.a: The tool uses the date you enter in “Age as of” as its reference date. When it matches the birthday in that year, “Days to birthday” shows zero days.
